    • ParameterSensitivityQuality

      private ParameterSensitivityQuality(ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.ParameterDefinition parameter, ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.AppliedFiniteDifferenceStencil stencil, double requestedStep, double coarseStep, double fineStep, double objectiveRelativeDisagreement, double[] constraintRelativeDisagreement, ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.EvaluationResult baseResult, List<ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.SensitivityPerturbation> perturbations)
      Creates immutable parameter-level sensitivity evidence.
      Parameters:
      parameter - parameter definition
      stencil - actual bounded stencil
      requestedStep - requested step
      coarseStep - actual coarse step
      fineStep - actual fine step
      objectiveRelativeDisagreement - objective derivative disagreement
      constraintRelativeDisagreement - constraint derivative disagreements
      baseResult - base process evaluation
      perturbations - perturbation evidence

    • isAllEvaluationsFeasible

      public boolean isAllEvaluationsFeasible()
      Checks whether the base and every perturbation satisfied hard constraints.

      An infeasible perturbation does not by itself make a finite-difference derivative numerically invalid. It is retained as explicit engineering evidence for callers that require sensitivities wholly inside the feasible process region.

      Returns:
      true when all evaluations were feasible

    • getPerturbations

      public List<ProcessModelSimulationEvaluator.SensitivityPerturbation> getPerturbations()
      Gets immutable perturbation evidence.
      Returns:
      perturbations in evaluation order

    • isNumericallyStable

      public boolean isNumericallyStable(double relativeTolerance)
      Checks step-halving consistency against a caller-selected tolerance.

      This is a numerical consistency check, not a physical-validity or shadow-price certificate. Feasibility is reported separately by isAllEvaluationsFeasible().

      Parameters:
      relativeTolerance - finite non-negative maximum relative disagreement
      Returns:
      true when all evaluations converged and every derivative comparison is within tolerance

    • maximumFiniteDisagreement

      private static double maximumFiniteDisagreement(double objectiveDisagreement, double[] constraintDisagreements)
      Returns the largest disagreement, preserving non-finite comparisons as incomplete evidence.
